issue_context.title: Support for choosing bcrypt version/ident with password_hash filter
issue_context.body:
### Summary

While setting up sonarqube and automating setting the admin password directly in the database, I noticed that their bcrypt implementation is outdated and only supports the 2a version, while the password_hash bcrypt filter using passlib defaults to the latest version (2b).

I'd like to set the ident parameter of passlib bcrypt function from the password_hash filter (like with rounds).

Right now I'm doing this:
```yaml
    - name: encrypt password
      command:
        cmd: python3 -
        stdin: |
          from passlib.hash import bcrypt
          print(bcrypt.using(rounds=12,ident="2a").hash("{{ admin_password }}"))
      register: tmp
```
as a workaround.

Obviously, sonarqube should upgrade their bcrypt version, but ansible should also be able to handle this.

Passlib doc: https://passlib.readthedocs.io/en/stable/lib/passlib.hash.bcrypt.html#

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

password_hash

### Additional Information

```yaml
password: "{{ admin_password | password_hash('bcrypt', rounds=12, ident='2a') }}"
```

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct

@nuth Thanks for reporting this feature. Password hashing formats (like `sha256_crypt` and `sha512_crypt`) apart from `bcrypt` do not provide `ident` configuration.

> @nuth Thanks for reporting this feature. Password hashing formats (like `sha256_crypt` and `sha512_crypt`) apart from `bcrypt` do not provide `ident` configuration.

I realize this, same as many hashing algorithms doesn't support `rounds`, which is supported. I suppose you could make the ident part of the hash name, so that you end up with `bcrypt` (whatever default passlib has), `bcrypt_2a`, `bcrypt_2b` etc.
@nuth Could you please check if #74595 works for you and let me know? Thanks.

Perfect! Thanks for the quick fix :)

review_comments: Should this default to using `2b` since it doesn't suffer from "rare security flaws" like `2a`?
I think this will break backward compatability. I suggest we do this change in separate PR with porting guide entry.
